messages.content: Can you retrieve the weather forecast for White Plains for next week with temperatures in Celsius?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the tool `requests_get` with appropriate params.

The user wants "weather forecast for White Plains for next week with temperatures in Celsius". We have to use Open-Meteo API. Need coordinates for White Plains. Let's approximate: White Plains, NY ~ lat=41.0535°N, lon=-73.7622°W. Provide query parameters accordingly. For daily forecasts maybe we want temperature_2m_max/min etc. Use parameter "daily": ["temperature_2m_min", "temperature_2m_max"] plus "timezone".

Also specify units as metric? Actually open-meteo uses param "hourly" but also can set "forecast_days"? Wait open-meteo has "start_date" and "end_date" optional. But easier: just get daily min/max for next 7 days starting today. So start_date=today, end_date=+7days. We'll provide "latitude", "longitude", "daily": [...], "current_weather":true? Not needed. Also "timeformat" maybe not necessary.

But the tool expects only certain fields: url, headers, timeout, params includes latitude, longitude, elevation. It doesn't support other query parameters like daily. However the description says "Query parameters for the GET request." Only those three keys defined. That seems incomplete. Maybe they omitted others inadvertently. In typical usage, you'd pass all required query parameters via this dict. Since it's typed, we might still add additional ones beyond defined? Might cause error if strict typing. But likely allowed because JSON schema may accept unknown properties. I'll assume we can supply extra keys.

Thus we'll construct:

URL: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast"

Params:
{
   latitude: 41.0535,
   longitude: -73.7622,
   daily: ["temperature_2m_min","temperature_2m_max"],
   timezone:"America/New_York",
   start_date: today's date e.g., "2026-05-19"
   end_date: "2026-05-26"
}

We'll also set "units" maybe not needed since default is metric. Temperature will be in °C.

Let's compute dates: Today May 19 2026. Next week inclusive? Usually next 7 days including tomorrow through Sunday? We'll do start_date=2026-05-20, end_date=2026-05-27. Or simply start_date=2026-05-20, end_date=2026-05-27. That's 8 days though. Hmm.

Better: start_date=2026-05-20, end_date=2026-05-27 gives 8 days. To get exactly 7 days after today, we could set start_date=2026-05-20, end_date=2026-05-26. That's 7 days. Good.

So produce output.

Now let's craft the function call.
